title: Water trapped between bars
summary: After rain, water fills the dips between rocks; walk in from both ends carrying the tallest rock seen to total the water.
goal: Total the water held between the rocks

mapping.story: Tallest rock each walker has passed

examples.label: Twelve rocks
examples.explanation: Six units of water settle in the dips.

examples.label: One big basin
examples.explanation: Water rises to 4 across the basin.

examples.label: Rising rocks
examples.explanation: Water runs off; nothing is trapped.

ladder.name: Scan both sides of every rock
ladder.idea: For each rock, find the tallest rock to its left and to its right; the water above it is the lower of the two minus its own height.

ladder.name: Precompute the tallest on each side
ladder.idea: Fill one list of tallest-so-far from the left and one from the right, then add up the water at each rock.
ladder.insight: The tallest rock to the left of position i is just the tallest to the left of i − 1, or rock i itself. One pass computes all of them.

ladder.name: Two walkers from the ends
ladder.idea: Walk in from both ends, each carrying the tallest rock it has passed. The walker on the lower side settles its rock's water and steps inward.
ladder.insight: If the left walker's tallest is lower than the right side, the left rock's water is limited by the left tallest alone; the right side cannot lower it. So we never need the full tables.

transfer.problem: Along a city skyline, find how much snow settles on rooftops lying between taller buildings, given each building's height.
transfer.explanation: Each rooftop holds up to the lower of the tallest buildings on either side; walk in from both ends carrying those maxima.

selfCheck: Water above a rock is the lower of the two side maxima minus its height.
Moves the walker on the lower side.
Returns 0 when nothing can be trapped.
